newsitem.title: CANADA: Blizzard shuts down southern Manitoba.
newsitem.headline: Blizzard shuts down southern Manitoba.

text.p: A spring blizzard that has dumped more than than 35 cm (over a foot) of snow shut down southern Manitoba this weekend.
"All the highways (in southern Manitoba) are closed," said a spokeswoman of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police on Sunday afternoon. They had been closed on Saturday as well.
She said plows still had not gotten out to the highways and were unlikely to do so until the winds, which have been gusting to 80 km per hour 50 mph died down.
Between 500 and 1,000 commercial trucks cross the Canada- U.S. border each day at Emerson, Manitoba, where RCMP ordered the closure of Highway 75.
A recording at a government office in Winnipeg that reports on road conditions to the public said it would remain closed because of the snow.
Winds were strong enough to blow some cars off highways, the Canadian Press news agency said, citing the police.
